cumleler: What do your eyes do when you look out of a train?
Optokinetic nystagmus, or OKN, is a normal nystagmus while watching moving stripes.
As stripes move right, the slow phase follows them to the right.
The fast phase returns the eye left, as on a train ride.
Normally, responses to rightward and leftward motion are symmetric.
Marked asymmetry suggests a central problem and is reported to the physician.
